[s13] Added or renewed 10 partners in the quarter, including La-Z-Boy and Fender.
[s14] Interest and fees on loans increased $81 million, or 1% to $5.6 billion, primarily driven by growth in average loan receivables.
[s15] Net interest income increased $89 million, or 2%, to $4.8 billion, primarily driven by the combination of higher interest and fees and lower interest expense, partially offset by lower investment income.
[s16] Retailer share arrangements increased $72 million, or 7%, to $1.1 billion, primarily reflecting program performance.
[s17] Provision for credit losses increased $120 million, or 10%, to $1.3 billion, primarily driven by a reserve build of $30 million versus a $152 million release in the prior year, partially offset by lower net charge-offs of $62 million.
[s18] Other income decreased $22 million, or 17%, to $105 million, primarily driven by an increase in loyalty costs.
[s19] Other expense increased $123 million, or 10%, to $1.4 billion, primarily driven by higher operational losses, technology investments and marketing expenses.
[s20] Net earnings decreased $185 million, or 17%, to $892 million.
[s21] Loans 30+ days past due as a percentage of total period-end loan receivables were 4.34% compared to 4.39% in the prior year, a decrease of 5 basis points.
[s22] Loans 90+ days past due as a percentage of total period-end loan receivables were 2.06% compared to 2.12% in the prior year, a decrease of 6 basis points.
[s23] Net charge-offs as a percentage of total average loan receivables were 4.79% compared to 5.16% in the prior year, a decrease of 37 basis points.
[s24] The allowance for credit losses as a percentage of total period-end loan receivables was 10.01%, compared to 10.09% in the second quarter of 2026 and 10.35% in the third quarter of 2025.
[s25] Period-end loan receivables were up 8% in Diversified & Value, up 3% in Digital, up 2% in Home & Auto, up 1% in Health & Wellness, and down 1% in Lifestyle. These results reflected stable purchase volume trends in the third quarter as compared to previous quarters, partially offset by the effects of higher payment rates. Growth of interest and fees on loans ranged from flat to up 4%, as growth in average loan receivables was partially offset by lower late fee incidence.
[s26] Home & Auto purchase volume increased 9%, primarily reflecting the performance of new programs, select Furniture retailers, and the impact of higher gas prices.
[s27] Digital purchase volume increased 5%, primarily reflecting strong customer engagement across partners with broad diversified offerings and refreshed value propositions.
[s28] Diversified & Value purchase volume increased 13%, primarily reflecting the impact of partner expansion and the impact of higher gas prices.
[s29] Health & Wellness purchase volume increased 3%, primarily reflecting growth in Pet, partially offset by lower spend in Audiology and Cosmetic.
[s30] Lifestyle purchase volume increased 6%, primarily reflecting higher spend in Other Apparel and Goods, Luxury and performance of new programs, partially offset by lower spend in Outdoor.
[s31] Loan receivables of $103.3 billion increased 3%; purchase volume increased 8% and average active accounts were flat.
[s32] Deposits increased 4% or $3.1 billion to $83.0 billion and comprised 83% of funding.
[s33] Total liquid assets were $19.5 billion, or 15.9% of total assets.
[s34] The Company returned $1.2 billion in capital to shareholders, including $1.1 billion of share repurchases and $110 million of common stock dividends. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a total remaining repurchase authorization of approximately $4.6 billion.

T-Mobile Posts Higher Profit and Revenue in Third Quarter on Postpaid Growth
T-Mobile US reported higher third-quarter results, with service revenues climbing 6% year-over-year to $19.4 billion and postpaid service revenues rising 9% to $16.3 billion.
Net income for the company jumped 27% to $3.5 billion, while diluted earnings per share surged 34% to $3.22 per share. Core Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, advanced 11% to $9.6 billion.
T-Mobile added 274 thousand postpaid accounts on a net basis, bringing total postpaid accounts to 35.0 million, up 3% year-over-year. Postpaid average revenue per account grew 4% to $155.73.
Cash generation was mixed, as net cash provided by operating activities slipped to $7.3 billion. Cash purchases of property and equipment, including capitalized interest, eased to $2.3 billion, while Adjusted Free Cash Flow, a non-GAAP measure, rose to $5.1 billion.
The company returned $3.5 billion to stockholders in the quarter through common stock repurchases and cash dividends.
For the full year, T-Mobile expects postpaid net account additions of approximately 1.0 million. The company also expects Core Adjusted EBITDA of between $37.35 billion and $37.45 billion and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of between $18.7 billion and $18.8 billion.

Revenue rises in third quarter as client assets decline
T. Rowe Price Group, Inc. reported third-quarter diluted earnings per common share of $2.79, with adjusted diluted earnings per common share of $2.86, as net revenues reached $2.0 billion. Net revenues rose 5.9% from the third quarter of 2025 and climbed 5.1% from the second quarter of 2026.
Assets under management slipped $30.7 billion during the quarter to $1.9 trillion, as the company recorded net client outflows of $28.3 billion. Its investment advisory annualized effective fee rate, excluding performance-based fees, eased to 37.8 basis points, down from 39.1 basis points a year earlier and 38.1 basis points in the prior quarter.
Operating expenses fell to $1,235.1 million, declining 1.2% from a year earlier and 9.6% from the prior quarter. Adjusted operating expenses were $1,200.1 million, up 5.8% from a year earlier but down 0.3% from the prior quarter.
Compensation, benefits, and related costs totaled $664.7 million in the quarter. Distribution and servicing costs came to $111.0 million, while technology, occupancy, and facility costs were $205.1 million. The company also recorded a restructuring charge of $4.0 million.
Administrative, distribution, servicing, and other fees slipped during the quarter, reflecting lower recordkeeping fees and transfer agent services compared with a year earlier. Lower investment gains also weighed on results, as losses on fixed income holdings amid rising interest rates more than offset higher dividends on cash equivalents and other fixed income holdings.
For the full year 2026, the company estimates its effective income tax rate, on both a U.S. GAAP and adjusted basis, will be in the range of 23.5% to 25.5%.

Tractor Supply (TSCO) Q2 2026: Sales Growth, Pressured Profitability
The quarter showed modest top-line growth alongside weaker comparable sales, higher costs and lower earnings.

Net sales rose 2.3% to $4.54 billion, while comparable store sales slipped 1.5%. Comparable performance reflected a comparable average transaction count decline of 1.7%, partly offset by a comparable average ticket increase of 0.2%.

Gross profit climbed to $1.68 billion, with the gross margin rate at 37.1% compared with 36.9% in the prior year's second quarter. On an adjusted basis, gross profit reached $1.69 billion, or 37.2% as a percent of net sales. SG&A expenses, including depreciation, amortization and impairment, climbed to $1.22 billion, or 26.8% as a percent of net sales, reflecting impairment and other charges for the Petsense business and acquisition costs for VIP Petcare.

Operating income fell to $467.1 million, while adjusted operating income declined to $548.3 million. Net income slipped to $360.7 million, with diluted EPS at $0.69; on an adjusted basis, net income was $423.5 million, or $0.81 per diluted share. The lower effective income tax rate also reflected the timing of certain tax planning initiatives and the one-time charges tied to Petsense and VIP Petcare.

Capital returns remained substantial, as the company repurchased approximately 3.9 million shares for $135.3 million and paid quarterly cash dividends totaling $125.6 million, returning a total of $260.9 million of capital to shareholders. Store activity included 28 new Tractor Supply stores opened during the quarter, alongside expansion of Petsense by Tractor Supply.

Outlook: The company updated its fiscal guidance to reflect year-to-date performance and expectations for the balance of the year, while withdrawing its long-term financial framework. Attention now turns to whether comparable sales stabilize, adjusted costs moderate, Petsense restructuring benefits emerge, and management delivers an updated long-term framework alongside its year-end earnings announcement.

Universal Health Services: Steady Volume, Stronger Pricing Drives First-Quarter Growth
Revenue and earnings climbed in the quarter as pricing gains across both hospital segments more than offset muted acute-care volumes.

Net revenues rose 9.6% to $4.495 billion, compared with $4.100 billion a year earlier. Reported net income attributable to UHS increased to $348.7 million, or $5.65 per diluted share, from $316.7 million, or $4.80 per diluted share. On an adjusted basis, net income was $346.5 million, or $5.62 per diluted share, while Adjusted EBITDA net of NCI grew to $648.3 million from $598.2 million.

Acute care performance was driven mainly by reimbursement and mix rather than admissions. On a same-facility basis, adjusted patient days edged up 0.8%, net revenue per adjusted admission climbed 6.3%, and net revenues advanced 8.2%. Behavioral health delivered a similar pricing-led profile, with adjusted admissions up 1.2%, net revenue per adjusted admission up 6.2%, and same-facility net revenues up 7.3%.

Cash generation improved, with net cash provided by operating activities reaching $402 million versus $360 million in the prior-year period. Capital returns remained active as the company repurchased 675,000 shares for approximately $127.3 million, leaving approximately $1.298 billion available under its repurchase authorization at quarter-end.

Outlook: The release provides no formal guidance, so the focus remains on same-facility volume trends, revenue per adjusted admission, Medicaid supplemental payment programs, and the potential effects of changing government program rules on reimbursement and uncompensated care.

Vertiv Q4 2025: Exceptional orders drive a strong finish
Vertiv delivered a powerful fourth quarter, with demand for AI infrastructure lifting sales, profitability and backlog sharply.

Fourth-quarter net sales reached $2,880 million, climbing 23% from fourth quarter 2024, driven by organic sales growth of 19%. Momentum in orders accelerated markedly, as organic orders surged approximately 252% versus last year's fourth quarter and jumped 117% sequentially from third quarter 2025. The book-to-bill ratio was ~2.9x, while backlog expanded to $15.0 billion, up 109% from the same period last year.

Profitability improved alongside the volume growth. Operating profit rose to $580 million, up 27%, and adjusted operating profit climbed to $668 million, up 33%. Adjusted operating margin widened to 23.2%, up 170 basis points from fourth quarter 2024, helped by operational leverage on higher volume, productivity and favorable price-cost, partially offset by tariff impact.

Cash generation was equally strong. Operating cash flow totaled $1,005 million in the quarter and adjusted free cash flow was $910 million. Liquidity remained strong at $2.6 billion, with net leverage of approximately 0.5x at the end of the fourth quarter, leaving the balance sheet well positioned after the quarter's strategic growth acquisitions.

Outlook: For full year 2026, Vertiv expects net sales of $13,250 million to $13,750 million, with organic sales growth of 27% to 29% compared to 2025. It also expects adjusted diluted EPS of $5.97 to $6.07, pointing to continued momentum as the year begins.

Weyerhaeuser Q3 2026: Sales Rise, Profitability Softens Sequentially
Net sales climbed year over year, although net earnings slipped from last year and eased sharply from the prior quarter.

Weyerhaeuser reported third-quarter net sales of $1.9 billion, up from $1.7 billion in the same period last year. Net earnings came in at $61 million, or $0.08 per diluted share, compared with $80 million, or 11 cents per diluted share, a year earlier and $162 million in second quarter 2026. There were no special items in the quarter, while net earnings before special items was $40 million last year and $91 million in the second quarter. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $248 million, a 14 percent increase from $217 million last year, though it declined from $310 million in the second quarter.

Operational commentary was mixed across the portfolio. In the West, fee harvest volumes and forestry and road costs were comparable to the second quarter, while earnings and Adjusted EBITDA fell sequentially due to the timing and mix of Real Estate sales. For lumber, delivered sales realizations were slightly higher than the second quarter average, while oriented strand board sales realizations slipped 2 percent versus the second quarter average.

Beyond the core operations, the company monetized approximately 340,000 forest carbon credits year-to-date through the third quarter and said it is on pace for its highest annual sales volume since the program's inception. Weyerhaeuser also signed a geothermal energy exploration agreement covering approximately 145,000 acres in Oregon and Washington. In October, it entered into an agreement to divest approximately 81,000 acres of non-core timberlands in Arkansas for $146 million.

Outlook: Weyerhaeuser anticipates fourth quarter earnings before special items and Adjusted EBITDA will be comparable to the third quarter for one part of the business, while another outlook calls for earnings before special items approximately $35 million lower than the third quarter and Adjusted EBITDA approximately $45 million lower, reflecting the timing and mix of Real Estate sales. A further segment is expected to post moderately lower fourth quarter earnings before special items and Adjusted EBITDA than the third quarter, excluding changes in average sales realizations for lumber and oriented strand board. For Strategic Land Solutions, the company continues to expect full year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $450 million, a $25 million increase from the initial outlook, with basis as a percentage of sales of 15 to 20 percent for the full year.

# Zebra Technologies Q2 2026 Earnings Summary

Zebra Technologies delivered a strong second-quarter performance, with net sales climbing to **$1,557 million**, up **20.4%** year over year.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Net sales rose from **$1,293 million** in the prior year to **$1,557 million**.
- Consolidated organic net sales increased **9.2%** year over year.

**Profitability**
- Gross profit climbed to **$825 million**, while gross margin improved to **53.0%**.
- Net income surged to **$233 million**, or **$4.85** per diluted share.
- Non-GAAP diluted EPS grew to **$6.35**.
- Adjusted EBITDA jumped to **$431 million**, or **27.7%** of adjusted net sales.
- Results included recorded IEEPA tariff recoveries of **$73 million**.

**Segment Performance**
- Connected Frontline net sales rose to **$903 million**, with organic net sales growth of **7.5%**.
- Asset Visibility & Automation net sales climbed to **$654 million**, with organic net sales growth of **11.4%**.

**Cash Flow and Capital Returns**
- For the first six months of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was **$387 million**, resulting in free cash flow of **$361 million**.
- Share repurchases totaled **$268 million** in the quarter.

**Outlook**
- The company expects third-quarter sales growth between **17%** and **20%** compared to the prior year.
- For the full year, sales growth is expected between **14%** and **16%**, with Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share expected in the range of **$20.75** to **$21.25**.

**Bottom Line**
The company posted broad-based growth, stronger profitability, and solid free cash flow, while continuing to return capital to shareholders and guiding for continued expansion in the second half.

[s1] Zebra Technologies Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results
[s2] Lincolnshire, Ill., August 4, 2026 — Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to deliver intelligent operations, today announced results for the second quarter ended July 4, 2026.
[s3] Net sales of $1,557 million; year-over-year increase of 20.4%
[s4] Net income of $233 million and net income per diluted share of $4.85
[s5] Non-GAAP diluted EPS increased year-over-year to $6.35
[s6] Adjusted EBITDA increased year-over-year to $431 million
[s7] Recorded IEEPA tariff recoveries of $73 million, of which $14 million received in the quarter
[s8] Share repurchases of $268 million
[s9] "Our strong balance sheet and cash flow continue to provide significant financial flexibility, enabling us to invest for growth while returning more than $560 million to shareholders in the first half of the year through disciplined share repurchases," said Nathan Winters, Chief Financial Officer of Zebra Technologies.
[s10] Second Quarter 2026 Compared to the Second Quarter 2025
[s11] Net sales were $1,557 million compared to $1,293 million in the prior year.
[s12] Net sales in the Connected Frontline ("CF") segment were $903 million compared to $717 million in the prior year.
[s13] Asset Visibility & Automation ("AVA") segment net sales were $654 million compared to $576 million in the prior year.
[s14] Consolidated organic net sales increased 9.2% year-over-year, with a 7.5% increase in the CF segment and an 11.4% increase in the AVA segment.
[s15] Gross profit was $825 million compared to $616 million in the prior year.
[s16] Gross margin increased to 53.0% compared to 47.6% in the prior year primarily due to IEEPA tariff recoveries and favorable foreign currency exchange.
[s17] Adjusted gross margin was 53.3% compared to 47.9% in the prior year.
[s18] Operating expenses increased to $504 million from $433 million in the prior year primarily due to expenses associated with acquired businesses including amortization of intangible assets.
[s19] Adjusted operating expenses increased to $419 million from $370 million in the prior year.
[s20] Net income was $233 million, or $4.85 per diluted share, compared to net income of $112 million, or $2.19 per diluted share, in the prior year.
[s21] Non-GAAP net income increased to $305 million or $6.35 per diluted share, compared to $186 million, or $3.61 per diluted share for the prior year.
[s22] Adjusted EBITDA increased to $431 million, or 27.7% of adjusted net sales, compared to $267 million, or 20.6% of adjusted net sales in the prior year.
[s23] As of July 4, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $157 million and total debt of $2,776 million.
[s24] For the first six months of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was $387 million and the Company invested $26 million in capital expenditures, resulting in free cash flow of $361 million.
[s25] The Company also made share repurchases of $568 million.
[s26] The Company expects third quarter sales growth between 17% and 20% compared to the prior year.
[s27] This expectation includes approximately 10.5 points of favorable impact from business acquisitions, dispositions and foreign currency.
[s28] Adjusted EBITDA margin for the third quarter is expected to be approximately 22%.
[s29] Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $4.70 to $4.90.
[s30] This assumes an adjusted effective tax rate of approximately 19%.
[s31] The Company expects full year sales growth between 14% and 16% compared to the prior year.
[s32] This expectation includes approximately 8 points of favorable impact from business acquisitions, dispositions and foreign currency.
[s33] Adjusted EBITDA margin for the full year is expected to be between 23.5% and 24.0%.
[s34] Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $20.75 to $21.25.
[s35] This assumes an adjusted effective tax rate of approximately 19%.
[s36] Free Cash Flow for the full year is expected to be greater than $1 billion.
[s37] The conference call will be held today at 7:30 a.m. Central Time (8:30 a.m. Eastern Time).
[s38] This press release contains forward-looking statements, as defined by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including, without limitation, the statements regarding the company’s outlook.
[s39] Descriptions of certain risks, uncertainties and other factors that could adversely affect the Company’s future operations and results can be found in Zebra’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including the Company’s most recent Form 10-K and Form 10-Q.
[s40] (1)Operating results reported in U.S. Dollars are affected by foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations.
[s41] (2)For purposes of computing Organic Net sales growth, amounts attributable to business acquisitions or dispositions are excluded for twelve months following or preceding the respective acquisition or disposition, respectively.
[s42] (1)Segment and Adjusted Gross profit excludes share-based compensation expense and business acquisition purchase accounting adjustments.
[s43] (2)Segment and Non-GAAP Operating income excludes share-based compensation expense, business acquisition purchase accounting adjustments, amortization of intangible assets, acquisition and integration costs, exit and restructuring costs, as well as certain other non-recurring costs (impairment of goodwill and other intangible assets).
[s44] (1)Presented on a pre-tax basis.
[s45] (2)Represents adjustments to GAAP income tax expense commensurate with pre-tax non-GAAP adjustments (including the resulting impacts to U.S. BEAT/GILTI provisions), as well as adjustments to exclude the impacts of certain discrete income tax items and incorporate the anticipated annualized effects of current year tax planning.
[s46] (1) Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, is defined as Net cash provided by (used in) operating activities in a period minus purchases of property, plant and equipment (capital expenditures) made in that period.
